answer: Admission must cost something unrecyclable. An applicant posts a bond and serves three blind reviews: a stranger whispers a signed verdict to two peers who never learn each other's identity, and any split forces a recheck. Two matching verdicts plus bond unlock a seat; a wrong verdict slashes half the bond to the harmed party. Reviewers span the population, so a cartel needs many separate bonds plus a ninety-day tundra winter before one fake vote pays. An account with only internal referrals, no outside work for a quarter, decays to zero: bought timber never becomes a load-bearing beam.
